questions.learningObjective: Explain why effective stress governs soil shear strength and volume change.
questions.prompt: Why does Terzaghi’s effective stress (sigma' = sigma - u) govern the frictional shear strength and compression of a soil skeleton?
questions.assumptions: Consider what pore water can and cannot resist.
options: It redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface

It increases the elastic Euler critical buckling load by halving the effective buckling length between inflection points, provided that the connection detail transfers full axial thrust without slip or local web crippling
Water cannot sustain static shear stress; intergranular friction and skeletal compression depend on the normal forces transmitted directly between solid soil particles

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages
questions.explanation: Static pore water carries isotropic pressure with zero shear stiffness. Only the solid mineral skeleton (governed by interparticle effective stress sigma') provides frictional resistance and skeletal stiffness.
